item.title: Reading a Local Forecast Under Uncertainty
item.description: Read the fictional town of Alder Vale’s bulletin on Saturday river levels. Distinguish what the model predicts, how much its results vary, and what the stated probabilities mean for a decision about the riverside route.

children.definition: A group of simulations with deliberately varied inputs or model settings, used together to examine possible outcomes.
children.example: In Alder Vale’s Saturday bulletin, the ensemble contains 40 simulations, each showing a possible course for the river through the day.
children.translation_uz: kirish maʼlumotlari yoki sozlamalari oʻzgartirib bajarilgan model sinovlari toʻplami

children.definition: A single execution of a simulation using a particular set of inputs and settings.
children.example: One model run in the Alder Vale bulletin puts the river above 3.0 metres by noon under its particular starting assumptions.

children.definition: The process of setting the starting state of a simulation before it calculates what may happen next.
children.example: For initialization, the Alder Vale model uses the latest river-gauge readings and estimates of how wet the soil is.

children.definition: A period or area for which measurements that would normally inform an analysis are missing.
children.example: An observation gap overnight left the Alder Vale team without upstream gauge readings for three hours.

children.definition: The level of geographical detail a model can represent, often expressed as the distance between neighbouring grid points.
children.example: At the model’s spatial resolution, the two bends just upstream of Alder Vale fall within the same grid cell.
children.translation_uz: modelning fazoviy tafsilotlarni ajrata olish darajasi

children.definition: The span from the reference time of a prediction to the furthest point in the future it covers.
children.example: The Friday evening bulletin has a prediction horizon of 30 hours, taking its river projections through to midnight at the end of Saturday.

children.definition: A single value chosen to represent the middle or typical outcome among the possibilities considered.
children.example: The bulletin gives 2.7 metres as the central estimate for Saturday’s highest river level, using the median of the simulated peaks.

children.definition: The degree to which numerical results from different simulations differ from one another.
children.example: The bulletin shows a wider spread for Saturday evening than for Saturday morning, as the simulated river levels diverge later in the day.

children.definition: A value corresponding to a specified percentage position in an ordered distribution.
children.example: In the bulletin's distribution of possible Saturday peaks, the 90th percentile is 3.2 metres, so the model puts 90% of the probability at or below that level.

children.definition: A range intended to contain a future observed value with a stated probability under the assumptions of the statistical method.
children.example: The bulletin’s 80% prediction interval for Saturday’s peak runs from 2.2 to 3.2 metres, leaving a combined 20% probability below or above those bounds under the model.

children.definition: An instance of a measured or simulated quantity going above a specified level.
children.example: For the riverside route, the bulletin counts a simulated peak of 3.01 metres as an exceedance of the 3.0-metre limit.

children.definition: A number expressing the chance that a specified event will occur.
children.example: The bulletin gives an event probability of 25% for the river rising above 3.0 metres on Saturday, so the route coordinator keeps both outcomes in mind.

children.definition: The degree of agreement between predicted probabilities and observed frequencies across many comparable cases.
children.example: To check calibration, the Alder Vale team examines whether the river went above the stated level in roughly one quarter of past cases assigned a 25% chance.
children.translation_ru: согласованность прогнозных вероятностей с наблюдаемыми частотами
children.translation_uz: prognozda berilgan ehtimollarning hodisa amalda qanchalik tez-tez yuz berishiga moslik darajasi

children.definition: A coherent account of how conditions could develop under a particular combination of assumptions.
children.example: In one scenario in the Alder Vale bulletin, heavier rainfall upstream coincides with already saturated soil, and the river rises sharply after midday.
